title: Sales Enablement Playbook — Positioning, Messaging, Competitive Briefs, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook is a consolidated, sales-facing reference for Redwood Inference positioning and messaging, competitive brief talking points, pitch-deck guidance, pricing yardsticks, representative case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. Use this in customer discovery, technical validation, and procurement conversations.

Intended audience: Sales (AE/SDR), Solutions Engineers, Sales Engineering Managers, Field Marketing, and Deals Desk.

Quick summary of Redwood value props (elevator pitches)

- For product/ML engineers: Redwood makes inference predictable and economical at production scale — consistent latency, lower unit cost via batching/caching, and a single API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- For platform & security teams: Redwood provides enterprise-grade controls (VPC/private deployment, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs) and SLA-backed dedicated capacity for regulated workloads.
- For engineering leaders: Redwood shifts operational risk away from owning inference — we provide predictable unit economics, rollout tooling, and observability for cost/quality tradeoffs.

Core messaging pillars (use in all customer collateral)

1) Production-first reliability and performance
- Latency SLOs and predictable throughput (hosted and Dedicated tiers).
- Automatic fallback and smart routing to maintain availability during capacity events.

2) Cost-aware controls and transparency
- Batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles tuned per workload.
- Token-level cost breakdown in Console; recommendations via Redwood Optimize.

3) Unified experience across deployment modes
- Same API and rollout semantics for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private.
- Eases migration from proof-of-concept to compliant production.

4) Developer-first UX + observability
- SDKs, quickstarts, per-model/per-route dashboards, and traceable regression alerts.

Competitive brief (short-form)

Competitors to call out:
- General cloud AI platforms (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI) — compete on breadth, integration with cloud services. Redwood differentiators: inference-first runtime optimizations, transparent unit economics, and unified runtime across private/on-prem.
- LLM API providers (Model-as-a-Service vendors) — compete on simplicity and managed models. Redwood differentiators: predictable latency at scale, dedicated capacity options, and enterprise deployment modes for regulated customers.
- Inference infra vendors (self-hosted runtimes like Triton or third-party orchestration) — compete on control. Redwood differentiators: fully managed runtime with smart routing, autoscaling, and production observability out of the box.

Competitive messaging templates (talking points)

- If customer cares about latency: "Redwood offers SLA-backed dedicated pools and a GPU-optimized serving runtime that reduces tail latency via continuous batching and kernel selection."
- If customer cares about cost: "We provide batching/caching and quantization profiles that typically reduce per-token cost by 30–60% compared to naively hosting on GPU fleets."
- If customer cares about compliance: "Redwood Private gives you a customer-controlled control plane, KMS/HSM integration, audit logging, and on-prem packaging for air-gapped environments."

Pitch deck: slide outline & guidance

Use this canonical outline for a 10–12 slide pitch tailored to engineering + security stakeholders. Keep a technical annex for SRE/infra reviewers.

1) Title & one-liner
2) Customer problem (latency/cost/operational risk) — customer metrics
3) Redwood solution overview (hosted, dedicated, private)
4) How it works at a high level (runtime, caching, smart routing)
5) Performance & cost outcomes (benchmarks relevant to prospect)
6) Security & compliance (Private, KMS, audit logs, certifications)
7) Integration & migration story (API parity, SDKs, quickstarts)
8) Deployment options & pricing summary
9) Case studies / references
10) Next steps & pilot proposal

Appendix: recommended technical slides to include where relevant
- Architecture diagram for Private deployment (networking, control plane, KMS)
- Throughput/latency benchmark charts for relevant model families
- Rollout plan: canary -> A/B -> full traffic flow

Pricing guidance (high-level, for commercial conversations)

Note: This section is guidance for AE + Deals Desk. Do not treat as legal pricing. Always confirm with pricing policy and finance for final quotes.

Summary of typical pricing constructs

Offering | Typical metric | Commercial levers
---|---:|---
Hosted API | per-token / per-embedding | volume tiers, reserved commit credits
Dedicated | committed monthly GPU capacity | term length (12/36 months), burst credits, SLOs
Private | platform licensing + support | license seat or node-based + professional services
Add-ons | observability retention, premium SLA | fixed monthly or usage-based

Guidelines for discounting and concessions
- Small POC: offer 3-month sandbox with limited free tokens and standard support.
- Enterprise pilots: typically 3–6 months with a modest committed spend to unlock Dedicated trial capacity.
- Seat/term discounts: escalate to Deals Desk for >20% list discount or multi-year commitments.

Example pricing yardsticks (internal, illustrative only)
- Hosted tokens: $0.0008 – $0.03 per 1K tokens (varies by model and deployment characteristics).
- Dedicated GPU pool: negotiated, common starts at $15k–$40k/month per dedicated GPU-equivalent depending on model throughput and SLA.
- Private licensing: one-time onboarding + annual platform fee (negotiated).

Sales motion & technical validation checklist

1) Discovery (AE)
  1. Identify personas: ML engineer, platform/SRE, security/compliance.
  2. Capture non-functional requirements: latency targets, throughput, data residency, encryption, expected peak qps.
2) Technical intro (SE)
  1. Share tailored pitch deck and a short benchmark summary.
  2. Validate model families, token budgets, and integration points.
3) Pilot / PoC (cross-functional)
  1. Define acceptance criteria: latency P99 < X ms, throughput Y rps, inference cost per 1K tokens <= $Z, or functional accuracy metrics.
  2. Select deployment mode: hosted sandbox, Dedicated trial, or Private eval.
4) Procurement & Legal
  1. Align on SLA, data processing addendum, and contract term.
5) Onboarding & rollout (Customer Success)
  1. Run onboarding checklist; configure monitoring and billing alerts.

PoC template (technical acceptance criteria examples)

- Sample acceptance criteria list (pick 3–5):
  - End-to-end P99 latency <= 200ms for short-form generation (<= 256 tokens).
  - Throughput >= 200 qps sustained with 95% of requests meeting latency target.
  - Cost per 1K tokens <= $X (agreed in advance).
  - Model outputs pass X% of quality checks on evaluation prompt set.

Case studies (short vignettes for slides and talking points)

1) Fintech SaaS ("NexaPay") — reducing latency and cost
- Pain: Customer-facing fraud detection model had unpredictable tail latency and high GPU cost.
- Solution: Redwood Dedicated with KV caching for common prefixes and model quantization profile.
- Outcome: 40% reduction in per-token cost and 3x reduction in P99 latency; integrated with NexaPay’s VPC for compliance.
- Quote to use: "Redwood cut our inference bill in half while improving checkout latency — our ops team finally sleeps at night." — Head of Platform, NexaPay

2) Healthcare enterprise ("MediCore") — private deployment and auditability
- Pain: Regulatory requirements required on-prem inference with strict key management and audit trails.
- Solution: Redwood Private with on-prem package, HSM-based KMS integration, and extended audit retention.
- Outcome: Successful SOC2 audit with Redwood in scope; pilot moved to full deployment.

3) Marketplace startup ("Textly") — fast time to market
- Pain: Needed rapid iteration and predictable scale for chat UX during growth.
- Solution: Redwood Hosted API + Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization.
- Outcome: Rapid launch in 3 weeks and 25% lower unit cost vs initial self-hosted experiment.

Security FAQ for prospects (concise answers for buyer-facing conversations)

Q: Where is my data stored and who can access it?
A: For Hosted customers, data is stored in region-specified cloud accounts; access to production data by Redwood employees is tightly controlled and only allowed for troubleshooting with customer approval. For Private deployments, control plane and data plane remain within customer-managed networks.

Q: Do you support encryption at rest and in transit?
A: Yes. All customer data in transit is TLS 1.2+; data at rest is encrypted with customer-managed keys where required (KMS/HSM integrations available for Dedicated/Private).

Q: What compliance certifications do you hold?
A: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and is in process for ISO 27001. For regulated customers, we provide evidence packages and can support third-party audits for Private deployments.

Q: How do you handle keys and secrets?
A: We integrate with customer KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and support HSM-backed keys for Private/on-prem deployments. Keys are never exported without customer authorization.

Q: How does Redwood protect model IP and customer prompts?
A: We enforce strict RBAC, audit logging, and data isolation per organization. For sensitive workloads we recommend Private deployment mode and can enable data retention and forwarding policies to match customer requirements.

Q: What is your incident & breach notification process?
A: Refer to our Incident Response Security runbook. We commit to notifying affected customers within contractual windows defined in the SLA and provide post-incident reports and remediation actions.

Q: Can we run Redwood in an air-gapped environment?
A: Yes. Our on-prem package supports air-gapped deployments; professional services can assist with installation and operations runbooks.

2) Tailor deck: SE pulls relevant benchmark slices and the appropriate deployment architecture slide.
3) Run PoC: Use PoC template; capture telemetry and acceptance criteria.
4) Close / onboard: Involve Customer Success for rollout and SSO/KMS integrations.

Maintenance notes

- This playbook should be reviewed quarterly or when we update pricing, launch new Dedicated features, or receive new compliance attestations.
- Send updates and suggested edits to the playbook owner.

Appendix: one-page objection responses (snippets)

- "Your costs will be lower with your own hosting": Response — "Self-hosting can be cheaper at very high scale, but requires significant SRE investment; Redwood provides optimized runtime and ongoing product improvements (kernel selection, KV caching, quantization) that often lower TCO and speed time-to-market."
- "We need full control of models": Response — "Redwood supports private/on-prem deployments with identical API semantics; we can run inside your VPC or on-prem with integrated KMS."
